Hi Aisha — great question and thanks for the clear asks. Summary below; I can also set up a short call with our security lead if you want to dig into evidence.

High-level summary (short bullets for procurement packet):
- Default hosted: inference executes in the region selected at project creation (by default US region). We run on major cloud providers (primary: AWS us-east-1 for hosted US workloads).
- Subprocessors: compute/on-demand GPUs run on AWS (US), GCP (EU fallback), and select edge partners for certain low-latency options. Networking/egress uses provider backbone and our CDN partners.
- Cross-border: we do not intentionally route US-hosted requests outside the selected region unless fallback capacity is required; fallbacks are governed by routing policy and require customer opt-in for cross-region failover.
- Retention/deletion (hosted): prompt & response content is kept in ephemeral runtime memory and KV caches for milliseconds to minutes; persisted logs/telemetry retained 90 days by default; customer-requested logs are retained per contract (can be 0 days). Physical deletion path: tombstone within 24 hours, primary storage purge within 30 days; backups have a 90-day TTL.
- Private/Dedicated: private deployments (VPC or on-prem) keep data in-customer environment; by default Redwood does not have access to message contents unless explicitly configured. KMS/HSM integrations available for key control.

I'll attach a short matrix and our SOC2 summary in my next message. Do you also need the full subprocessors list for each region (we can produce a region-specific roster)?

Hi Aisha — looping in our solutions and security leads and attaching a short compute-handshake diagram and SOC2 summary as requested. Key points and concrete answers below.

--- Concrete subprocessors by execution locus (US-hosted / EU-hosted) ---
- US-hosted (default when project/tenant is created in US region): primary compute + storage: AWS (us-east-1); object store and backups: AWS S3 (us-east-1); telemetry & observability: Datadog (US region).
- EU-hosted (if customer selects EU residency): primary compute: GCP (europe-west1) and regional object store; telemetry in EU; fallback compute still uses our EU provider pool unless explicit cross-region failover is enabled.
- Edge/latency partners: selected CDN+edge vendors operate in additional regions; these are only used for low-latency cache hops (not for long-term storage).

Note on cross-border behavior:
- Default behavior is to honor the residency selection. Our smart routing only sends requests outside the selected region in these cases: 1) customer has enabled cross-region failover, 2) capacity emergency where we've exhausted local reserved capacity and customer has agreed to fallback, or 3) explicit partner integration that requires multi-region processing.

KV cache and persistence:
- KV caches are in-memory by design and are not written to persistent disks in normal operation. Short-lived cache snapshots may exist transiently for warm-start optimizations but are ephemeral (sub-second to a few minutes) and are not replicated cross-border.
- Any logging, analytics, or customer-configured recording is persisted to region-aligned storage; backups are retained per the timelines below.

Encryption & key control:
- Hosted customers can use CMEK with our KMS integrations; we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or GCP KMS in the region of the tenant. HSM integrations available for Dedicated/Private.

Deletion timeline (hosted):
- Live runtime artifacts: ephemeral, cleared within minutes by default.
- Tombstone flag: within 24 hours of a deletion request (or retention expiry) an object is marked tombstoned and removed from active indexes.
- Primary storage purge: typically completed within 30 days after tombstone (may vary by storage tier).
- Backups/replicas: removed on a 90-day rotation; customers can shorten this via contract or use Private deployment for immediate erasure requirements.

Evidence & attachments:
- Attached: redwood_compute_handoff_matrix.pdf (single-page diagram of compute hops and subprocessors)
- Attached: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (controls summary and SOC2 audit window)
- Link: full subprocessors roster for each region is available here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Jk-example-drive-link (we can export a region-only CSV for procurement).
